cf.title: Remove redundant MultiXactIdIsRunning() check in HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdate()

input.subject: Remove redundant MultiXactIdIsRunning() check in HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdate()

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. The only one raised, maintenance-fit-1, was refuted because the retained comment states the dependency on the first check and multixact membership is a documented invariant. The patch removes a branch that message #1 argues cannot be reached, and one reviewer agreed in message #3. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and no committer has confirmed the reasoning.

brief.title: Remove redundant MultiXactIdIsRunning() check in HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdate()
brief.problem: In the HEAP_XMAX_IS_MULTI branch of HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdate(), a second MultiXactIdIsRunning() call follows an earlier one that already returns TM_BeingModified if any member runs. The author says the second call always returns false, so its else branch is dead code. This costs a multixact member lookup and a proc array scan when the updater aborted, and it makes the code harder to read.
brief.proposed_design: The patch removes the second MultiXactIdIsRunning() call and its unreachable TM_BeingModified branch. When the updater aborted, the code sets the HEAP_XMAX_INVALID hint bit and returns TM_Ok. v2 drops the "By here ..." comment and keeps the "There's no member ..." comment, as the reviewer asked.
author_claims: Multixact membership is immutable, and a member that was not running cannot become running again, so the second check always returns false.
Commit 05315498012 made the check redundant when it changed the first check back to cover all members.
The patch does not change behavior.
The patch avoids a multixact member lookup and a proc array scan when the updater aborted.
brief.thread_state: Chao Li agreed with the analysis and asked for a comment change, which v2 makes. No committer has replied, and the CommitFest entry is in Needs review.
unclear: The material does not say whether the first check and the second check run under the same buffer lock, or whether that matters here.
The patch shows no test or assertion that confirms the branch is never reached.
The author gives no measurement for the saved lookup and proc array scan.
The material does not say whether other visibility routines, such as HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC, have the same double check.

prior_attempts.title: Remove redundant NULL check in clause_selectivity_ext()
prior_attempts.quote: Certainly, such an assumption could be argued to be a bug they should fix; but I'm disinclined to make them jump through that hoop for a vanishingly small performance improvement.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane wanted the check kept because it is cheap and extensions call clauselist_selectivity and related functions and may rely on it not crashing on a NULL. He also said the list_length check proves nothing about NULL list elements, and that removing such checks one at a time without agreed invariants is not wise. David Rowley agreed, saying no speedup could be measured and no benchmark was given, and suggested marking the entry rejected.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 removed a defensive NULL check in a function that extensions call, so outside callers could depend on it. This patch removes a branch inside HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdate() that no caller can reach, because multixact membership is immutable.

refuted.title: Removed check leaves lockers unprotected if the first check narrows again
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch narrows the first check to the updater only, as 1ce150b7bb1 once did. With the second check gone, an aborted updater with live lockers now gets HEAP_XMAX_INVALID and TM_Ok, which drops row locks still held by running transactions. No test or assertion catches it.
refuted.argument: Message #1 shows this exact history: the second check and its else branch kept lockers safe while the first check covered only the updater. After the patch, the correctness of setting HEAP_XMAX_INVALID depends on the first check covering all members, and only a comment records that. Message #1 gives no measurement of the saving, and an aborted updater in a multixact is an uncommon path. [P2] was rejected for removing a cheap defensive check without agreed invariants, for a small gain.
refuted.author_must_show: Will v3 add an assertion under USE_ASSERT_CHECKING that no member is running before HEAP_XMAX_INVALID is set, so a future narrowing fails loudly?

precedents.title: Remove redundant NULL check in clause_selectivity_ext()

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a later patch to undo commit 05315498012 a few lines above the retained "There's no member ..." comment, which states the dependency. [P2] concerned extension callers of an exported function without agreed invariants, but multixact membership is a documented invariant.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch edits HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdate() in heapam_visibility.c, where setting HEAP_XMAX_INVALID now relies on the first MultiXactIdIsRunning() check alone.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch removes a multixact member lookup and proc array scan from the aborted-updater path of a tuple visibility routine.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Do both MultiXactIdIsRunning() calls run under the same buffer lock, and does the argument depend on that?
Do other visibility routines, such as HeapTupleSatisfiesMVCC, have the same double check, and should this patch cover them?
Is there a measurement of the saved member lookup and proc array scan, or is the patch justified by readability alone?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows heap tuple visibility and multixact handling would have to own it. No committer has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The committer signs for the claim that the removed branch is unreachable. If that is wrong, an aborted updater with running lockers gets HEAP_XMAX_INVALID and the row locks are lost.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 after the review comment in message #3, which made the requested comment change.

priority.reason: The patch is about 2 KiB in one file, tagged Refactoring Only, with no user-visible change and no measured gain. It needs a committer who knows multixact visibility to confirm the reasoning, and none has replied.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that nothing between the two checks can change the result rests on message #1 and message #3. The lock held across both checks could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make VACUUM remove MultiXacts with updater XIDs more eagerly
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes FreezeMultiXactId() so that VACUUM removes a MultiXact outright when all of its members are older than OldestXmin, instead of leaving it in place with FRM_NOOP processing. The goal is to get more use out of each GetMultiXactIdMembers() call and to remove more Multis that have updater XIDs, since OldestMxact can be held back much longer than OldestXmin.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread ends when Peter Geoghegan creates the CF entry. No message shows a reviewer objecting to this patch or the author explaining the withdrawal. Andres Freund's objections in the thread concern the separate patch that skips the TransactionIdDidCommit() sanity checks.

There's no point in setting up a context error callback when doing
conditional lock acquisition, because we never actually wait and so the

this is more in line with what ConditionalXactLockTableWait is doing.

Backpatch to 9.4, where this was added.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove redundant initializations
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Eisentraut proposed removing code that sets each struct field to zero right after makeNode() or memset() has already zeroed the whole struct. He kept initializations that carry nontrivial comments or keep symmetry between branches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback after waiting on author for three weeks: the patch no longer applied on HEAD, and no rebased version was posted. Before that, Tom Lane objected that explicit initialization of every field is an intended style, which helps when adding a new field and avoids depending on all-zero-bits values. Noah Misch later supported the idea and offered to review it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove redundant DISTINCT when GROUP BY already guarantees uniqueness
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Zsolt Parragi, Andres Taylor, David Rowley, Antonin Houska
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made the planner skip the DISTINCT step when a query has a plain GROUP BY (no GROUPING SETS), the clause is plain DISTINCT, and every GROUP BY key appears in the DISTINCT list. Each group yields one row, so the extra Sort and Unique nodes add no filtering.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers showed that v1 returned wrong results when the target list has a set-returning function, because SRF expansion happens after grouping but before DISTINCT. Reviewers also found that v1 matched keys by sort-group reference only and did not check opclass or collation. David Rowley judged the GROUP BY case too narrow and pointed to planner-wide UniqueKeys work instead. The author moved to the UniqueKeys patch series, then withdrew the entry after Antonin Houska pointed to newer and more complete unique-keys work posted elsewhere.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think only doing something just for that case is likely too narrow a scope.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid hiding shared filesets in pg_ls_tmpdir (pg_ls_* functions for showing metadata ...)
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_ls_tmpdir skips anything that is not a regular file, so it hides shared filesets, which are directories under pgsql_tmp. The proposal changes pg_ls_tmpdir to return an isdir column, as pg_stat_file does, so these directories show up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Both messages are from the author, and no reviewer reply appears in the visible messages.

precedents_retrieved.title: Align verify_heapam.c error message offset with test expectations
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes three error messages in contrib/amcheck/verify_heapam.c to report the successor tuple's offset (nextoffnum) instead of the current line pointer (ctx.offnum). A second part tightens the pg_amcheck test 004_verify_heapam.pl to expect the exact offset 43 instead of a \d+ wildcard.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Two reviewers agreed with the code fix, and no one objected. The author said he would not revise the test change further and left the decision to committers, and the thread ends there.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add pg_wait_for_lockers() function
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch exposes the lock manager's WaitForLockers() to SQL as pg_wait_for_lockers(), which waits for transactions holding given table locks, optionally in a single lock mode, to commit or roll back, without taking a lock itself. It supports incremental reading of inserted rows using pg_sequence_last_value(), as a replacement for briefly taking a conflicting lock with LOCK.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after off-list feedback from Robert Haas asking for more self-contained motivation, and after considering directly exposing GetLockers() and VirtualXactLock() instead. He planned to come back in a new thread with quantitative evidence that the function is more efficient than polling pg_locks. No reviewer had endorsed the patch in the visible messages during about 18 months of revisions.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Since the main advantage over polling the existing pg_locks view would be efficiency, we will try to provide more quantitative evidence/analysis of that. That will probably want to be a new thread and CF entry, so I'm withdrawing this one.

precedents_retrieved.title: Refactoring of heapam code
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal renames and moves heap-related code so that heap access method code is separate from generic relation code, starting with patches that split PageGetItem into heap and index variants and clean up names and comments in heapam.c, hio.c and catalog/heap.c. A follow-up wiki design draft proposed an API for primary storage access methods so that new heap-like table storage could be added.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Pavan Deolasee found that the first patch did not apply cleanly, and that PageGetItemHeapHeaderOnly() and PageGetItemHeap() looked identical. He expected the patches to be rewritten once the design discussion concluded. The design draft did not show how to handle row locking, page-mode reads, pruning, or executor access to system attributes such as xmax. The entry was returned with feedback, with fresh patches expected in a later commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Looks like a fine approach to me, but the API will need much more elaborate discussions. I am not sure if the interfaces as presented are enough to support everything that even heapam can do today.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server"
Reverted commit(s): Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server Previously, we skipped a checkpoint if no WAL had been written since last checkpoint, though this does not appear in user documentation. As of now, we skip a checkpoint until we have written at least one enough WAL to switch the next WAL file. This greatly reduces the level of activity and number of WAL messages generated by a very low activity server. This is safe because the purpose of a checkpoint is to act as a starting place for a recovery, in case of crash. This patch maintains minimal WAL volume for replay in case of crash, thus maintaining very low crash recovery time.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 18fb9d8d21a28caddb72c7ffbdd7b96d52ff9724.  Per
discussion, it does not seem like a good idea to allow committed changes to
go un-checkpointed indefinitely, as could happen in a low-traffic server;
that makes us entirely reliant on the WAL stream with no redundancy that
might aid data recovery in case of disk failure.

This re-introduces the original problem of hot-standby setups generating a
small continuing stream of WAL traffic even when idle, but there are other
ways to address that without compromising crash recovery, so we'll revisit
that issue in a future release cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY FREEZE and PD_ALL_VISIBLE
precedents_retrieved.summary:
COPY FREEZE and PD_ALL_VISIBLE
Threads: COPY FREEZE and PD_ALL_VISIBLE

roaster_notes.note: The one similar precedent [P2] died because extensions might pass NULL and no speedup was shown. That does not apply here: no caller can observe the removed branch, and the patch is mainly justified by readability. The missing measurement is a weak point but not a reason to reject; the thread reports no earlier discussion beyond the commit history in message #1.

The patch removes dead code inside HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdate() and changes no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog, pg_dump output, psql behavior or client-visible result. [P2] does not apply: its concern was extensions passing NULL to an exported function, and this patch keeps the function signature and its results unchanged.

The patch changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol or extension API. The only persistent effect is the HEAP_XMAX_INVALID hint bit, which is still set only after MultiXactIdIsRunning() has found no running member; it goes through the same SetHintBits() path, so checksum and standby behavior do not change.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It removes a redundant visibility check inside HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdate() and adds no SQL surface, privilege, setting or new information path, so no unprivileged user gains any ability or knowledge. Whether the branch is truly unreachable is a correctness question for other angles.

From the maintenance angle the change is small and local to one file, has no API, catalog or hot-path cost, and has nothing for an extension to depend on. The one concern above can be fixed with an assertion.

From the already-exists angle there is nothing to raise. The patch removes dead code inside one visibility routine and adds no feature, so no existing feature, extension or hook could already meet the need, and it adds no second mechanism. P2 is about removing a defensive check that extensions might rely on, and that reason does not apply to an internal branch shown unreachable.

The demand angle does not apply well here. The patch removes an unreachable branch in one internal function, adds no user-visible surface, and costs non-users nothing. Its main gain is readability, which needs no field demand. The speedup on the aborted-updater path is unmeasured, but the patch does not depend on it. [P2] does not fit: there, extensions could rely on the removed check, and no outside caller can reach this branch. Whether the branch is truly unreachable is a safety question for another angle.
